title: 48hr-role-handoff-brief
content:
Purpose:
This note is a compact, action-oriented "48 hour" handoff packet for managers, onboarding buddies, and People Ops when a candidate accepts an offer. The goal is to ensure the new hire has role context, clear first-week outcomes, and that outstanding interview evidence / risk items are visible and assigned before day one.

Scope:
Covers actions from offer-acceptance through the end of week one. Designed for technical IC and manager roles across product, infra, and platform; easily customizable for other roles. Not a full onboarding playbook — complements the standard New Hire Checklist.

Quick summary (what needs to be done in 48 hours):
- Finalize and share the 7-day orientation plan with the hire by email.
- Assign and notify the onboarding buddy.
- Confirm access requests (email, Slack, VPN, code review tools, cloud account) with SRE and IT.
- Publish a short role-context doc (one page) in the team drive with 3 priorities for the quarter and 3 immediate tasks.
- Surface any unresolved interview concerns and assign mitigations.

Manager checklist (owner: hiring manager) — deliverables to complete in 48 hours:
1) One-page role context (deliver as a doc and a single Slack DM):
   - Team mission in one sentence.
   - Primary metrics that role impacts (baseline + target).
   - Top 3 objectives for first 90 days.
   - Key collaborators and expected meetings (names + suggested agenda).
2) First-week plan (day-by-day):
   - Day 0 (pre-start): welcome email, calendar invites, equipment + access status.
   - Day 1: intro + team standup, buddy intro, environment setup, small first task.
   - Day 2–5: paired work, codebase orientation, first mini-deliverable definition, check-ins.
3) Interview evidence summary: add a 1-paragraph note for each core skill evaluated and identify any gaps that need early pairing.
4) Risk & mitigation register: list any concerns (skill, ramp risk, timezone, background checks) and immediate mitigations (pairing, shadow weeks, training modules).

Onboarding buddy checklist (owner: buddy)
- Confirm 30–60 minute introductory walkthrough on Day 1: dev environment, run tests, deploy flow.
- Prepare a short/cheap-win starter task that can be completed with guidance within 3 days.
- Compile a "cheat sheet" of 10 links: docs, team boards, repos, runbooks, dashboards.
- Be available for check-in end-of-day Day 1 and Day 3.

People Ops / IT checklist (owner: people-ops + IT liaison)
- Confirm asset request has been fulfilled (laptop spec, accessories, phone stipend).
- Create accounts and group memberships (Slack channels, Google groups, cloud IAM) — list specific groups.
- Trigger security awareness training and, if required, compliance enrollment (SaaS access attestation).
- Send benefits enrollment and payroll timeline.

Interview Evidence Ledger (required short entries — manager to paste in):
- Hiring rubric summary used at offer: list scored dimensions and notes.
  * Technical depth: 4/5 — strong systems design, flagged limited exposure to our infra stack (Go + CUDA pipelines).
  * Product sense: 3/5 — solid but prefers backend infra tasks; may need product domain pairing.
  * Communication: 5/5 — clear, concise, collaborative.
  * Culture fit & ownership: 5/5.
- Open questions from loop: familiarity with internal metrics pipeline; prior experience with quantized model serving.
- Recommended early mitigation: two paired sessions with infra engineer on week 1, and one focused training module on model serving primitives.

First-week learning objectives (measurable):
- Set up local dev environment and run test suite end-to-end.
- Ship a small change through CI to a staging branch with code review feedback incorporated.
- Demonstrate an understanding of the team's primary dashboard and the signal sources it consumes.
- Have a 1:1 with Product and outline a 30–60–90 learning plan.

Interview rubric snapshot (for manager archive) — key axes used to hire:
- System design (scoped to expected role level) — evidence: past designs, tradeoffs discussed.
- Implementation craft — code-quality, tests, debugging approach.
- Domain depth — model inference/runtime familiarity for infra-aligned hires.
- Collaboration & communication — cross-team interactions, ownership stories.
- Learning velocity — examples of quick ramp-up and self-directed learning.

Risk register (concise):
- Risk: limited exposure to CUDA / model quantization. Mitigation: schedule paired sessions + targeted training library link.
- Risk: onboarding overlap with release week (context switching). Mitigation: reduce initial task complexity and defer high-impact tickets until week 3.
- Risk: time zone mismatch for daily standups. Mitigation: asynchronous updates + shifted 1:1 cadence.

Decision log / outstanding approvals:
- Final laptop choice pending sign-off by SRE (owner: IT).
- Access to production dashboards requires two-factor onboarding; approval from security is pending (owner: manager).

Templates and copy-paste snippets (for manager):
- Welcome email subject: "Welcome to Redwood — first day details and quick links"
- Welcome email body (short): hi {name}, excited to welcome you. Your laptop will arrive by {date}. On day one we'll meet at {time} PT for intros. Here are 3 links to glance at before you start: [role one-pager], [team roadmap], [starter task].
- Slack intro template: "Please welcome {name}, joining as {role} on {start date}. {one-sentence role context}. Buddy: {buddy name}. Say hi!"

Follow-ups after first week (owner: manager + people-ops):
- 1-week check-in doc: short note from hire about blockers, confidence level (scale 1–5), and suggested adjustments.
- 30-day OKR draft: manager + hire collaborate on a realistic set of objectives for first 30 days.
- Feedback loop: schedule a 30-minute retrospective at day 14 to review ramp plan and adjust.

Notes & tips from People Ops:
- Keep the initial tasks intentionally small and high-signal. Small wins = confidence and momentum.
- Surface interview evidence in plain language; avoid verbatim question transcripts. Focus on what we learned about ability to do the role.
- If any background or employment verification flags appear, escalate immediately to People Ops (do not delay access provisioning for unrelated resources).

Appendix: example one-page role context (copyable)
- Team mission: "Make inference predictable and cheap for production apps."
- Role impact: "Reduce median tail latency of standard text-gen pipeline by 15% and own rollout for one performance experiment."
- 90-day goals: 1) Deploy a performance benchmark harness; 2) Ship two optimizations with measurable cost savings; 3) Pair on incident response runbook.
- First-week tasks: 1) Set up dev environment, 2) Run bench harness locally, 3) Triage a small regression ticket.

End of brief.

Document history:
- Drafted by: Aisha Patel (People Ops) 2025-11-05
- Reviewed with hiring manager: Liam Chen 2025-11-12
- Notes added: risk register and interview evidence 2026-02-18
